newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO official says peace needs U.S. pressure.
newsitem.headline: PLO official says peace needs U.S. pressure.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official said on Friday the United States must put pressure on Israel if Egypt's efforts to restart Middle East peace talks are to succeed.

"Egypt is doing its part out of a wish to save the peace process. Egypt's role needs American pressure on Israel because it (U.S.) is the only country that can practice such pressure," said Farouk Kaddoumi, who heads the PLO's political (foreign affairs) department.
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians broke down in March when the Jewish state began building a settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Egypt has recently taken on the mantle of main mediator in talks between Israel and the Palestinians after what Arabs have perceived as a loss of U.S. interest in the peace process.
President Hosni Mubarak's senior adviser Osama el-Baz has met separately with Palestinian and Israeli leaders several times in a bid to restart negotiations.

"The peace process has become completely frozen as a result of settlements, the measures undertaken by Israel and its provocative practices against the Palestinian people," Kaddoumi told reporters during a brief stop-over at Cairo airport.
He was on his way back to his headquarters in Tunis after a trip overseas.
"Continued provocative practices by Israel will lead to continued tension in the region and an increase in the series of violence because of delays in the peace process," he added.
Asked what he thought about a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution saying that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital, Kaddoumi, who is known for his tough stance, said:
"This resolution comes in the framework of increased measures taken by the American side to drown the peace process and destroy it completely.

"Unfortunately, the United States still regards the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) as a terrorist organisation despite the mutual recognition between the PLO and Israel. This position is further proof that Washington is not giving enough attention to the Middle East peace process," he added.
